newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chips gain as investors take heart.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chips gain as investors take heart.

text.p: Revived foreign investor interest pushed the Bratislava Stock Exchange higher on Thursday, as confidence began to slowly creep back into the market.
Dealers said parliament's approval on Tuesday of a new securities law that had been amedned to remove several controversial paragraphs had heartened investors.
"It looks as if foreign investors have regained confidence in the Slovak market after the passing of law," said dealer Libor Briska of Creditanstalt Bankverein.
The SAX index closed 6.58 points up at 175.05.

Penicilin-based drug producer Biotika headed the the blue chip advancers with an 80 crown rise to close at 910, followed by oil refiner Slovnaft, up 53 to 833, and steelmaker VSZ which closed up 37 at 567.
"I think this also reflects the fact that investors now recognises that many issues are undervalued," Briska said.
"I think there is still plenty of scope for growth both until the end of the year and in the beginning of the next."
Overall volume slid to 1,058,291 shares traded from 1,837,581 and turnover was 644.68 million crowns, down from 1.29 billion crowns on Wednesday.
